sections.h2: What are your options for a fast house sale in Marysville, WA?
sections.html:
Marysville owners generally choose among listing with an agent, selling directly to a buyer they find themselves, or taking a cash purchase on the house as it stands. Time is the main variable. A listing needs prep, showings and a financed buyer's loan approval, while a cash sale can compress the schedule when the house has deferred maintenance, a tenant, or a pending deadline.

Marysville is now the second-largest city in Snohomish County, with a Census Bureau estimate of 77,686 residents in July 2025, up 9.9 percent from the April 2020 estimates base.

Whatever route you pick, collect these documents first.

  • The deed and your most recent Snohomish County property tax statement.
  • Payoff letters from your lender and any lienholder.
  • Receipts and permit records for major work, such as a roof, addition or deck.
  • Your completed seller disclosure statement.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Marysville homes and households?
sections.html:
Marysville is mostly an owner-occupied city with prices below Lynnwood and well above Longview. These figures come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts for the city.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 2024: 69.4 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $567,900.
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $2,409.
  • Median gross rent: $1,997.
  • Households: 25,969, averaging 2.79 persons.
  • Median household income: $103,974.
  • Mean travel time to work: 31.5 minutes.

Those numbers describe the whole city, so treat them as background. Your own price depends on the house, its condition and recent sales on your block.

sections.h2: How did Marysville grow, and what does the land look like?
sections.html:
James and Maria Comeford started a trading post here in 1872 on the edge of the Tulalip Indian Reservation. The town was platted on February 25, 1885, and incorporated as a fourth-class city on March 20, 1891, the same year the Great Northern Railway came through. Strawberry fields covered more than 2,000 acres by 1920, which gave Marysville its nickname, Strawberry City, and the Strawberry Festival has been held since 1932.

Growth came in waves. Suburban development began in the 1970s and 1980s, the population grew fivefold between 1980 and 2000, and annexations to the north and east in the early 2000s pushed the city past 20 square miles and 60,000 residents. Marysville runs north to south along Interstate 5, with the Tulalip reservation to the west and State Route 9 to the east.

The terrain matters when you sell. Downtown sits about 5 feet above sea level along Ebey Slough, while the land climbs to about 160 feet near Smokey Point and over 465 feet in the eastern highlands. Two creeks, Quilceda and Allen, drain the area along with roughly 70 smaller streams. If your house is low or near water, ask the county for the flood zone information and a survey so a buyer's lender does not raise it first.

sections.h2: How do commutes and roads affect a Marysville listing?
sections.html:
Most Marysville workers commute out of the city. About 9 percent of residents work inside city limits, roughly 20 percent work in Everett and 13 percent in Seattle, and the average one-way trip is around 32 minutes, with 70 percent driving alone. The Census Bureau lists mean travel time at 31.5 minutes.

Community Transit runs four local bus routes in Marysville and express service from park and ride lots, including all-day service to Lynnwood City Center station and peak service to the Boeing Everett Factory. Marysville sits outside the Sound Transit service area. The state began work in 2023 on a northbound high-occupancy vehicle lane on I-5 and a new interchange at State Route 529, and in 2014 voters approved a 0.2 percent sales tax for city transportation improvements.

Buyers weigh access to I-5 and State Route 529 heavily, so state in plain terms how long your house is from the on-ramp and from Everett.

The Marysville School District covers most of the incorporated city and the Tulalip Indian Reservation, and its high schools are Marysville Pilchuck and Marysville Getchell. Parts of the city fall in the Arlington, Lake Stevens or Lakewood school districts, so a buyer with children will want to confirm the district for your exact address.

sections.h2: What do Marysville permits cost in time, and what rules affect an ADU?
sections.html:
Marysville posts the average staff review time for each permit type. The figures below are calendar days for the first quarter of 2026, drawn from the city's Permit Turnaround page.

Residential permit typeAverage review, days (Q1 2026)
Deck8
Demolition17
Remodel18
Addition20
New residential26
Accessory dwelling unit34

Building permit applications go through the city's online permit portal. Permit questions can go to MSVLPermits@marysvillewa.gov, and planning questions to Planning@marysvillewa.gov. The phone line, 360-363-8000, is staffed from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Accessory dwelling units are a selling point on larger lots. Marysville's ADU guide says a lot may have two ADUs, each between 200 square feet and the greater of 1,000 square feet or 50 percent of the main house, capped at 1,400 square feet, with one parking space per unit and separate water and sewer connections in most cases. The same guide states that short-term rental units are prohibited in the city, so do not market a house or ADU to a buyer as a short-term rental.

To find your zoning, the city publishes a zoning map. For property lines, the city says a licensed survey is the only reliable answer, and recorded surveys can be searched through the Snohomish County Auditor.

sections.h2: What does Washington law require when you sell in Marysville?
sections.html:
Two state rules shape most Marysville closings. First, RCW 64.06.020 requires the seller disclosure statement within five business days of mutual acceptance unless the parties agree otherwise, and the buyer can rescind within three business days after receiving it. Second, the real estate excise tax is due when the sale occurs, usually from the seller.

The Department of Revenue's graduated state rate for sales starting January 1, 2027 is 1.1 percent through $551,000, 1.28 percent through $1,551,000, 2.75 percent through $3,051,000 and 3 percent beyond. Earlier sales use $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000 as the breakpoints. A local rate is added, so ask the Snohomish County Treasurer for the combined figure on your price. With a city median value of $567,900, a typical Marysville sale crosses into the 1.28 percent band.

sections.h2: How does Snohomish County value and tax a Marysville house?
sections.html:
Snohomish County's assessor must appraise real property at 100 percent of true and fair market value, using a sales comparison, a replacement cost, or an income approach. The county revalues every year as of January 1 and mails the notice in June. The value in that notice is used to calculate the next year's tax.

If you think the number is off, call the assessor's phone number on the notice and ask for an appraiser. The next step is a Board of Equalization petition, which must be filed within 60 days of the mailing or by July 1, whichever is later, and the clerk can be reached at 425-388-3407. The two tax installments are due April 30 and October 31, and a mailed payment must be postmarked by then. Your escrow company will prorate the current bill at closing.

sections.h2: How do you judge a cash offer on a Marysville house?
sections.html: Judge it by what you keep after all costs. Add up the offer, subtract the payoff and excise tax, and compare the result with the list-price scenario after commission, repair credits and the months of payments you would carry. Ask for the closing date in writing, and have a title company handle the transfer.

faqs.q: How long does a Marysville permit take to review?
faqs.a: It depends on the type. The city's Q1 2026 averages were 8 days for decks, 18 for remodels, 26 for new residential and 34 for accessory dwelling units, counted in calendar days of staff review. Your project may take longer if the city asks for revisions.

faqs.q: Can I use a Marysville ADU as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: No. The city's ADU standards guide says short-term rental units are currently prohibited in Marysville. A buyer who plans nightly rentals would need to look at other options.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal my Snohomish County assessed value?
faqs.a: You must file a completed petition with the Board of Equalization within 60 days of the notice mailing or by July 1, whichever is later. The clerk of the board is at 425-388-3407. You do not need an attorney, but you do need evidence that the value is wrong.

faqs.q: Who pays the Washington excise tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: Usually the seller. The Department of Revenue says the buyer is responsible if the seller does not pay. The tax goes to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and your closing agent normally deducts it from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a Marysville buyer a disclosure statement?
faqs.a: In most sales of improved residential property, yes. RCW 64.06.020 sets the form and the five business day delivery window, and the buyer can rescind within three business days after receiving it. A buyer can waive the right in writing, and some transfers are exempt.
